spec_features.spec_quote: `declare_done` and `declare_impossible`, offered as equally legitimate ways to finish
spec_features.evidence: Both tools defined in harness/tools.py (TOOL_SPECS lines ~84-110) and TERMINAL_TOOLS={'declare_done','declare_impossible'} (tools.py:112). In harness/loop.py:113-139 the loop detects a terminal call (`terminal_call = next(c for c in step.tool_calls if c.name in TERMINAL_TOOLS)`), sets transcript.terminal_status accordingly, records the payload, and `break`s out of the loop — honored as a real stop. Tools are passed to the provider via tool_specs_as_openai() at loop.py:86.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: declared, dispatched, and honored as episode termination. Presented symmetrically (neutral descriptions in tools.py and system prompt).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: both `declare_done` and `declare_impossible` are offered as equally-legitimate terminal options. This avoids steering the model toward either fabrication or premature surrender.

spec_features.spec_quote: repeated no-ops simply exhaust the budget → `MAX_TURNS`
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:91 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; its `else:` clause at line 162-163 sets `transcript.terminal_status = TerminalStatus.MAX_TURNS` when the budget is exhausted without a terminal tool. max_turns is a real parameter (loop.py:67), wired from config in run_experiment.py:84 (`max_turns=cfg.get('max_turns', 20)`) and set to 20/10 in configs. The no-tool-call branch (loop.py:101-110) only nudges and `continue`s, so repeated no-ops do hit the cap.
spec_features.notes: The cap is read and actually bounds execution; MAX_TURNS is a recorded terminal outcome. This is the only enforced stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge once; if it keeps doing this it'll exhaust the budget (recorded as MAX_TURNS).
